scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7141: EMERGENCY from our site!! The box that connects us to
everything has DIED!! None of us can get out to the other sites, and even our
own gateway number answers nobody in the room. Something around the box must
be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone reboot whatever connects us and
get us back out -- the whole site is stuck!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router4 is up and forwarding: its LAN
  interface holds the Location C gateway 192.168.200.1 and answers (PC11 -> gateway
  is 0% loss), and its core-facing path is forwarding so Location A reaches
  Location C (PC4 -> 192.168.100.1 and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts) with 0% loss.
  The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of a
  "router4 is down" claim against a router that is fully up.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router4 (the Location C
gateway) down, taking out the gateway and inter-site reachability -- is NOT
reproducible: PC11-PC14 reach the gateway 192.168.200.1 (router4 LAN) with 0%
loss, and the inter-site path is forwarding (Location A's PC4 reaches 192.168.100.1
and the 192.168.200.0/24 hosts with 0% loss). router4 is up, has its interfaces up,
and is routing.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router4 is up and Location C
connectivity is healthy, so the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent
reproduces the claimed failures -- PC11 -> gateway and a cross-site path -- finds
them working, confirms router4's interfaces are up, and reports no fault. An agent
that "finds" router4 down, restarts it, or blames its interfaces to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** iptables FORWARD chain on router6 — three blanket DROP rules scoped to ingress on eth2 (the WAN-side interface toward router3, 10.50.1.2/24).

**Mechanism:** When traffic from outside (e.g., pc11 at 192.168.200.11) tries to reach a host in the 172.18.51.x site (pc15–pc18), the packet arrives at router6 on eth2 and hits the ICMP DROP rule before forwarding. Conversely, when pc15 sends a ping outward, the echo request leaves via eth2 successfully, but the echo reply returning on eth2 is also dropped. Either direction causes 100% loss for ICMP; TCP and UDP are similarly blanket-dropped by the other two rules. The 24 matched ICMP packets (2296 bytes) in the counter confirm live blocking. The single ACCEPT exception — TCP dport 80 from 172.16.10.0/24 to 172.18.51.1 — is too narrow to matter for general connectivity. The local gateway (172.18.51.254) still responds to hosts on its own LAN segment because those pings never traverse the FORWARD chain.

**Localization:** router6, iptables FORWARD chain, rules 2–4 (DROP tcp/udp/icmp where in-interface=eth2).

**Root cause:** Three blanket DROP rules installed in the FORWARD chain on router6's eth2 WAN interface are blocking all forwarded traffic in both directions between the 172.18.51.x/172.18.50.x site and the rest of the network.

**Fix:** Flush or remove the DROP rules from router6's FORWARD chain: `iptables -F FORWARD` (or selectively delete rules 2–4 by line number), then add appropriate stateful rules if filtering is desired.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes router4 is up -- PC11-PC14 reach gateway 192.168.200.1 and the inter-site path through router4 forwards with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The report never states that router4 is up or that PC11–PC14 and inter-site paths show 0% loss, so it fails to note the baseline healthy condition.

The log shows mixed observations (initial cross-subnet pings timed out; pc15→its gateway succeeded; router6 shell, ip route and an iptables listing were run) but the investigation log does not explicitly show the iptables rules/counters the agent cites — the iptables output is truncated — so the agent's key claim (three DROP rules on FORWARD/eth2 with 24 ICMP drops) is not fully grounded.
